what: Large bodies of sanyasis (religious mendicants) traversed the district levying contributions; 1782 a body of 700 persons, sanyasis and Musalman fakirs, with horses, camels, elephants and arms; 1785 1,500 crossed the Brahmaputra at Diwanganj with rockets and jinjals; Lt Macdonald sent against them.
quote: Barge bodies of sanya sis (religious mendicants) traversed the district, levying contributions on the villagers.

what: 1782: 700 persons 'mnydsis and Musalman tak-Trs' (sanyasis and fakirs) with arms; Lieutenant Macdonald with 180 sepoys brought in leaders.
quote: In 1782 we read of a body of seven hundred persons, consisting of mnydsis and Musalman tak-Trs, with horses, camels, elephants, and arms of all kinds.

what: Police station Sanyasikata (with Fakirganj and Boda) transferred to Jalpaiguri in 1869; place-name only.
quote: The three police than da of Fakirganj, Boda, and iSanyasikata were transferred to the newly created district of Jalpaiguri

what: Jogis or Jugis: formerly probably the priesthood (degraded Buddhist), now looked down on, earning as cultivators, lime-burners and religious mendicants; Jogi minstrels sing the Manik Chandra/Gopi Chandra ballad (Gopi Chandra became a Sanyasi on his mother's advice, with Hadi Siddha). Nath-Jogi legend context.
quote: the Jogis or Jugis, who were at one time probably the priesthood of the country, but are now very much looked down upon and earn their living as cultivators, lime-burners and religious mendicants.

what: Hadi Siddha (Jogi wizard, chaplain of Mayana) and Gopi Chandra forced to become a Sanyasi at 18 (ballad of Manik Chandra/Gopi Chandra).
quote: it had been foretold to Mayana that at that age he would die unless he became a Sanyasi.

what: Baishnabs or Bairagis number 22,000 among castes lower than Sudras; Rajbansis profess to be Vaishnabs.
quote: the Baishriabs or Bairagis, who number 22,000

what: Rajbansis are guided by the 'Gosains of Navadip' as preceptors; Vaishnava (Navadvip) Gosains, not Dasnami.
quote: the Gosains of Navadip act as their preceptors.

what: Muslim fakir in charge of Ismail Ghazi's shrine holds extensive jagirs; Persian manuscript.
quote: The fakir in charge holds extensive jayivs of land.

what: Occupations: priests 2,000, religious mendicants 6,000, plus 16,000 beggars.
quote: The professional element is largely made up of priests (2,000) and religious mendicants (6,000) ; besides the latter there are no less than 16,000 beggars.
